mechanism_claims.claim_text: Spgillcin177-189 is source-supported as a membrane-disruptive peptide in S. aureus and P. aeruginosa, with microscopy, membrane-component inhibition, and permeability assays supporting membrane integrity damage.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: Spgillcin177-189 against S. aureus and P. aeruginosa
mechanism_claims.limitations: The record keeps membrane disruption as a supported mechanism class without claiming a single exclusive molecular target.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Spgillcin177-189 treatment is source-supported as increasing intracellular reactive oxygen species in the bacterial systems tested.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: Spgillcin177-189 against S. aureus and P. aeruginosa
mechanism_claims.limitations: ROS accumulation is recorded as an observed downstream mechanism-associated phenotype, not the sole lethal event.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Serial-passage assays locally support no resistance selection for the tested MRSA and MDR P. aeruginosa conditions under Spgillcin177-189 exposure.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Resistance findings are limited to the tested strains and local serial-passage design.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Local source material supports biofilm inhibition and extracellular S. aureus clearance in RAW 264.7 culture supernatant assays.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: Spgillcin177-189 anti-biofilm and cell-supernatant bacterial burden assays
mechanism_claims.limitations: These functional results are not promoted to in vivo therapeutic efficacy.

extraction_scope: Worker-6 mechanism adjudication from XML result sections, figure captions, PDF text, and DataSheet_1 supplementary text.

caution_findings.evidence_context: Mechanism claims are limited to membrane disruption, permeability, ROS, resistance-passage, biofilm, and cell-supernatant assays present in local sources.
